name: High-vol short-momentum reversal (violent down-leg fade)
rationale: THESIS: short-horizon NEGATIVE momentum reverses only in high-vol regimes — a sharp multi-day drop during elevated vol is an overshoot that overcorrects and bounces, whereas the same drop in a calm regime is the orderly start of a downtrend that continues. We fade a violent down-leg: ret_Nd below a fitted negative floor (SIGNED, used as a return so gt/lt on the signed value is legitimate) ARMED by realized vol above a fitted high-vol floor (vol_realized BOUNDED). DISCONFIRMER: (1) drop the vol_realized>floor gate (fade every short-term dip) — if high-vol-armed is not better risk-adjusted net of fees the vol gate is decorative; (2) run the IDENTICAL negative-momentum fade armed by LOW vol — it should LOSE, proving the regime SIGN (not just having a gate) is what carries the edge. This is the inverse-sign counterpart to the low-vol trend specs.
catalyst: A sharp short-horizon drop (negative multi-day return) coincides with elevated realized vol — a violent overshoot to the downside primed to overcorrect.
